body: Looks like a bug in the mypy plugin for attrs, as indicated by the failing `assert`. I can't help you further except to suggest that you read the code, and run it with `print()` calls added (or trace it using a debugger like `pdb`) to figure out how it works.
Worth noting that the reason the stack trace is nicer on master than in the release is that the release is using a mypyc-compiled binary.

This is the same as https://github.com/python/mypy/issues/6493 but with `dataclasses` -> `attrs`, the two plugins are very similar, so the existing PR that fixes the other issue can be easily updated to fix also this one, see https://github.com/python/mypy/pull/6644.

issue.title: Dataclasses: support mutable properties
issue.body:
Skip over attributes that are redefined as properties on dataclass construction.

As far as I understand, not redefining a symbol within the same scope is a fundamental assumption in mypy. However, I have not been able to figure out another way to get a mutable property that is also part of the `dataclasses.fields`. It seems that we are falling within the cracks in the sense that the property methods actually mask the attribute with the desired functionality and all seems to go well in the end. 

Any indications on how to make a cleaner implementation would be most welcome!

Fixes #6493

issue.title: Fix crash on overriding with frozen attrs
issue.body:
Fixes #6715 

Fix is straightforward, currently we assume that if we have a variable in MRO, and its name appears in current class, it is from this class, which in fact may not be the case when a variable is overridden with a property or method.

I also add a test case for a crash that was previously reported in the same issue but is already (accidentally?) fixed.
